# Krate

> AI can make the app. Krate makes it shippable: one tiny file, no per-app
> installer, Mac, Windows, Linux, permissions before it runs, and Cloud
> publishing.

Krate is the software file for the AI era. Krate Studio detects the AI tools
already on a computer, lets the person choose one, and turns a plain request
into a `.krate` app. The same file opens on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Before
any app code runs, Krate shows what the app wants to access and the runtime
enforces the person's decision.

Krate is open source and in public beta. The current release is v0.1.50, with
versioned releases shipping continuously for six desktop targets (macOS,
Windows, Linux, each on Intel and ARM). Krate Cloud is live with real
apps anyone can run in one click.

Key facts, all measured and published rather than estimated:
- A .krate app is a WebAssembly component compiled from Rust: no bundled
  browser, no per-app runtime. A playable game is 13 KB and the notes app used
  in the published benchmark is 37 KB.
- A markdown editor rebuilt in Krate and benchmarked against MarkText
  (Electron) on the same machine: 37 KB vs 271 MB installed, opens in about
  0.2 seconds vs 1.8 seconds, holds a 50,000-line document in 95 MB of
  memory vs 2.3 GB. Methodology at krate.tech/reports.html.
- Permissions are capability-based and enforced in code: an app declares
  what it needs, the person sees it in plain words before first run, and a
  denied capability is structurally unreachable. An app that organizes
  folders cannot even name a folder -- it asks the person to pick one, and
  the pick is the grant.
- AI authoring works with the tools people already have: Claude Code, Codex
  CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok CLI, or any tool via MCP.
  Krate Studio is the desktop app around the whole flow: describe, build,
  run, publish.
- Publishing is one click; every published app is content-addressed and can
  be run directly from its URL: `krate run https://hub.krate.tech/a/<id>`.

"No installer" means no installer for each app. A person installs Krate once.
Every `.krate` file after that opens like a document. Krate is not an HTML file
and not Docker. HTML is for browser apps. Docker packages server environments.
Krate packages a local desktop app for a person to open and control.

## Main pages
- [Krate](https://krate.tech/): what it is, install, and the numbers
- [Krate Store](https://krate.tech/cloud/): live gallery of published apps
- [Krate Studio](https://krate.tech/studio/): the desktop app
- [Docs](https://krate.tech/docs/): the book
- [Measurements](https://krate.tech/reports.html): every claim with its method
- [FAQ](https://krate.tech/faq.html)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/incyashraj/krate): source, tests, public bug board
